recommendation.summary: dsh-feishu-bot@0.19.16 (repo PlutoKeating/dsh-lark-bot) is a dsh profile-bundle plugin that bridges DeepSeek Harness into Feishu/Lark over an outbound WebSocket, with a QR-code first-run binding. Node intent: README prerequisite and engines.node both require Node.js >= 22.19, and CI (ci.yml, release.yml, cf-pages.yml) configures Node 22 with pnpm 10.33.0; no other Node major is named in the bounded evidence, so Node 22 is selected as the CI-tested major satisfying the declared engine minimum. No explicit author Node recommendation beyond the engines minimum was found. The manifest declares dsh.client.platform=web, and the README names the default adapter `sdk` with switchable `acp` / `headless` / `web`, so all four planes are recorded, with sdk primary. The author's validated DSH baseline is 0.1.0-rc.8 (README compatibility section, COMPATIBILITY.md matrix row, and dshWorkshop.compatibility), which is a documentation claim and differs from the Radar DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 runtime; the author's own real probe (scripts/probe-dsh-compat.mjs) was not run here. Development-only pnpm.overrides pin dsh core packages to 0.1.0-rc.8 and are not transferred to a consumer profile. Two documented disabled modes (DSH_LARK_DISABLED=1 stops the bridge engine; DSH_LARK_GUARDIAN_DISABLED=1 stops the guardian) are retained as additional limited comparisons for the web plane. Real Feishu binding, credentials, guardian/service lifecycle, in-chat commands and outbound IM channels remain explicit coverage gaps.

conclusion.statement: feishu-bot (artifact sha256 53692cc42a65e2857215603f930d8a0885a7e4ea48b8c51a6026f00f9747c34b, Node 22) was re-run after the protobufjs dependency-build approval. Native DSH 0.1.0-rc.8 (feishu-bot-node22-dsh-c38bca47e523) is compatible: the exact artifact installed, registered, loaded and satisfied its direct Node peer contracts. Native DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 (feishu-bot-node22) is unknown: its load phase timed out at 180s after entering external account authorization, and the one-time login evidence was withheld, so no pass is claimed. Web/TUI surfaces are surface-incompatible on both baselines: on 0.2.0-rc.1 the declared plugin client entry is absent from the DSH boot manifest (host passed, surface failed), and on 0.1.0-rc.8 the exact DSH Web profile exited with code 1 before exposing an HTTP surface (dsh-app-boot: 'user patch-layer watching requires the Cordis HMR service'), so surface and interaction stages were skipped. Adapters: initialize-compatible on 0.1.0-rc.8 for acp, headless and sdk; on 0.2.0-rc.1 headless and sdk are initialize-compatible while acp (feishu-bot-node22-acp-e221349d43ed) is initialize-failed because the published author CLI did not establish its adapter initialize handshake. All 8 tasks executed with 0 failures and 0 deferred/blocked cells.
coverageNotes: No real Feishu authentication, model generation, user task, resume, guardian service, or outbound message was exercised for any adapter cell; external account/QR/one-time login cannot be completed on the user's behalf and is recorded as an explicit coverage gap, not as plugin incompatibility.

Native DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 (feishu-bot-node22) is unknown, not passing: the load phase hit the 180s timeout while awaiting external account authorization, so no compatibility claim is made for that baseline.

Web/TUI surface incompatibility on 0.1.0-rc.8 is a DSH host boot failure (Cordis HMR service requirement in dsh-app-boot 0.1.0-rc.8), observed identically across three independent surface runs; it is not attributable to the plugin artifact.
Web/TUI surface incompatibility on 0.2.0-rc.1 is a manifest-level gap: the declared plugin client entry is absent from the DSH boot manifest, so interaction stages were skipped rather than failed.
acp adapter on DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 failed only at the initialize handshake; no further diagnosis of that handshake was possible with the available actions.

recommendation.summary: dsh-feishu-bot@0.19.16 (repo PlutoKeating/dsh-lark-bot) is a dsh profile-bundle plugin that bridges DeepSeek Harness into Feishu/Lark over an outbound WebSocket, with a QR-code first-run binding. Node intent: README prerequisite and engines.node both require Node.js >= 22.19, and CI (ci.yml, release.yml, cf-pages.yml) configures Node 22 with pnpm 10.33.0; no other Node major is named in the bounded evidence, so Node 22 is selected as the CI-tested major satisfying the declared engine minimum. No explicit author Node recommendation beyond the engines minimum was found. The manifest declares dsh.client.platform=web, and the README names the default adapter `sdk` with switchable `acp` / `headless` / `web`, so all four planes are recorded, with sdk primary. The author's validated DSH baseline is 0.1.0-rc.8 (README compatibility section, COMPATIBILITY.md matrix row, and dshWorkshop.compatibility), which is a documentation claim and differs from the Radar DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 runtime; the author's own real probe (scripts/probe-dsh-compat.mjs) was not run here. Development-only pnpm.overrides pin dsh core packages to 0.1.0-rc.8 and are not transferred to a consumer profile. Two documented disabled modes (DSH_LARK_DISABLED=1 stops the bridge engine; DSH_LARK_GUARDIAN_DISABLED=1 stops the guardian) are retained as additional limited comparisons for the web plane. Real Feishu binding, credentials, guardian/service lifecycle, in-chat commands and outbound IM channels remain explicit coverage gaps.
